summary: American speechwriter, pundit and three-time presidential candidate Pat Buchanan defended Nazi war criminals, echoed Holocaust denial and pushed white-nationalist, anti-immigrant politics into the Republican mainstream from the 1960s to the Trump era.

evidence.note: birth in Washington DC to a family with Confederate Mississippi roots
hired by the Nixon campaign in 1966, start of main span
memo to Nixon pushing Herrnstein's hereditary IQ claims about Black people
defends accused SS war criminals and steers Reagan's Bitburg visit
long David Duke segment: Klan, Louisiana seat, 1992 run
Willis Carto, the Populist Party and the Spotlight embrace Buchanan
1992 convention speech declaring a religious and cultural war
1996 run on blocking foreign workers, forcing anti-immigrant planks
Trump's 2000 Reform Party challenge attacks Buchanan as a bigot
Palm Beach County ballot miscount in the 2000 election, end of main span
Trump quotes a 2019 Buchanan border column; link to Christchurch

notes: Lifetime rule sets covered_span 1938-2019 (alive at release). main_span ends in 2000 with his last presidential run, though he kept writing columns; reviewer may prefer end null. Primary theme fascism-far-right over racism-white-supremacy because the pitch is mainstreaming the far right; nazism secondary for Holocaust denial and SS defence. Duke and Carto segments are substantial, so secondary.
